items.stem: A dataset is accurate but arrives six hours late every day, breaking morning reports. Which data quality dimension is failing?

options.rationale: Correct: the data is correct but not available when needed, which is a timeliness failure.
The values are correct, so accuracy is not the failing dimension.
No rows or fields are described as missing.

items.explanation: Correct: the data is correct but not available when needed, which is a timeliness failure.

items.stem: What does data lineage most directly enable during a quality incident?

options.text: Impact analysis of which downstream assets are affected by a bad source
options.rationale: Correct: lineage maps dependencies so you can trace a defect to every affected downstream asset.

options.text: Automatic correction of the bad values
options.rationale: Lineage shows relationships; it does not fix values.
Lineage is metadata, unrelated to compute capacity.
Encryption is a security control, not lineage.

items.explanation: Correct: lineage maps dependencies so you can trace a defect to every affected downstream asset.

items.stem: Which TWO checks are value-level data quality tests rather than schema-only checks? (Select TWO)

options.text: A not-null assertion on a required column
options.rationale: Correct: not-null validates actual values, catching missing data the schema may still allow.

options.text: A distribution check that flags an unexpected spike in nulls or outliers
options.rationale: Correct: distribution checks examine the data's statistical shape, a value-level concern.

options.text: Confirming the column exists with the declared data type
options.rationale: That is a schema check, not a value-level test.

options.text: Verifying the table name matches the catalog
options.rationale: That is metadata/schema validation, not a value-level check.

items.explanation: Correct: not-null validates actual values, catching missing data the schema may still allow.
